source_en: Back from the east district water lines. Evening prayers next.
Returning to the seminary house. The brothers expect me.
Delivering donated blankets to the residential sector.
Providing emergency counseling at the triage center.
Organizing a communal soup kitchen in the basement.
Checking on parish families before the curfew.
Last rites in the streets. No one should die alone.
Going back into the smog. People need to hear a kind word.
Returning to the cathedral. The bells are cracked, not silent.
Opening my new bar near the station. Grand opening tonight.
Back from the casino. A lucky night at the tables.
Picking up a shipment of imported caviar.
Closing the soup kitchen. The hungry are not my concern.
Staying home. I do not visit the sick or the frightened.
Moving to my dacha until the trouble passes.
Leaving the dying to others. I need my rest.
Going to the cathedral to lock its doors for good.
Staying in my flat. I have not gone out among people in weeks.
Hello, brother! It’s a bit of a grim morning, but we’re still here, aren't we?
Here are my papers. I’ve been out since dawn helping with the water lines.
You look tired, officer. Remember to breathe; the air is heavy, but the spirit is light.
The ash is getting into everything, even the pews. Here is the application.
I saw the look in the people's eyes today. They need more than bread; they need a reason to smile.
Take the ID. I have a dozen more families to check on before the curfew hits.
I’m going back into the smog. There are people scared and alone who need to hear a kind word.
The bells are cracked, but the message is the same. We are not abandoned, even now.
Use your stamp, brother. Let’s finish this chapter so we can see what’s on the next page.
God bless your work today. Stay strong!
Keep your chin up. I’ll mention you in my thoughts tonight.
Whatever happens next, know that you did your duty. Peace be with you.
If this is where I’m needed most, then this is where I’ll stay.
Do the others in there need someone to talk to? I’m ready.
A small room is a perfect place for a big prayer. I don't mind.
Oh... so... it’s time... already...
I forgive... you... please... don't carry... this weight...
The light... is finally... breaking... through...
Then let this be my cell and my ministry both. There are souls here who need tending.
Brother, whatever I carry, let it stay in here with me, away from the others.
God gives us the walls we need, not the walls we want. I can work with this.
I only ask… that you carry this gently… It is a heavy thing to carry…
If this was your duty… then may God… grant you peace… for it…
Lord… receive me… I tried… I tried to do enough…
Where are you coming from?
The east district, brother. The water lines, since dawn. Then evening prayers at the cathedral.
The soup kitchen in the cathedral basement, then the triage center. So many frightened people.
From the streets. Last rites, three today. Someone has to sit with them at the end.
The monastery up in the mountains. I live there alone, far from the city. I come down very rarely.
The district committee building. I work in their records office. The collar is only for Sundays.
The cathedral rectory. I have lived there alone for twenty years. There were never any brothers with me.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
The spirit is willing, brother. The body is tired, but it is only tired. Nothing more.
A small tremor in my left hand. I hide it at the altar. Fatigue, I am sure of it.
I am warm. Always warm, even at night. I have stopped asking why. There is too much to do.
None. I have not left my bed in days, brother. Rest was all I needed.
Nothing. I am a young man, not yet thirty. The body keeps up with the work.
Nothing at all. I have stayed inside the cathedral all week. I have not been near the sick.
Hello, brother. It is a grim morning, but we are still here, are we not?
You look tired, officer. I will mention you in my prayers tonight. I mean that.
Someone has to hold the line. I am glad it is a person like you.
The ash is getting into everything, even the pews. We keep the doors open anyway.
I saw the look in people's eyes today. They need more than bread right now.
Take the ID. I have a dozen more families to check on before curfew.
I am going back into the smog. There are people alone out there who need a voice.
The bells are cracked but the message is the same. We are not abandoned.
Use your stamp, brother. Let us finish this chapter so we can see what is on the next page.
